outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Advanced Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
outline.description: This introductory chapter contextualizes the current landscape of Large Language Models (LLMs) in mathematical reasoning. It defines the gap between closed-source frontier models and open-source alternatives, introduces the DeepSeekMath initiative, and outlines the core thesis: that strategic data curation and novel optimization algorithms can push open models to rival proprietary giants.
subtopics: The Challenge of Structured Reasoning: Why Math Differs from Natural Language Tasks
Current State of Art: Comparing GPT-4/Gemini-Ultra vs. Open Source Models
Overview of DeepSeekMath: Goals, Architecture, and Performance Benchmarks
Key Contributions Summary: High-Quality Web Data Mining and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Constructing the Foundation – Scalable Math Pre-Training
outline.description: An deep dive into the data engineering philosophy behind DeepSeekMath. This chapter explains how public web data was transformed into a massive, high-quality mathematical corpus, contrasting this approach with traditional reliance on arXiv or textbooks. It covers the technical specifics of filtering, deduplication, and quality validation.
subtopics: Limitations of Traditional Sources: Analyzing ArXiv vs. Web Data Effectiveness
The Iterative FastText Pipeline for Data Selection
Validation Experiments: Measuring Corpus Quality via Few-Shot Prompting
Multilingual Considerations: Integrating English and Chinese Mathematical Content
